newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech minister wants local partner for plane maker.
newsitem.headline: Czech minister wants local partner for plane maker.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Monday he would prefer a Czech investor win a government tender offering a 34 percent stake in the troubled light aircraft maker Aero Vodochody a.s..

"In my opinion, (the partner for Aero) should be a Czech investor, but this has not been pre-determined... The (government) does not explicitly say it would have to be a Czech party," Dlouhy told a news conference.
The cabinet assigned Dlouhy last week to draw up a list of criteria to pick a partner for the company by Christmas.

It also approved a three-billion crown debt restructuring deal for Aero, which is controlled by the state through state bank Konsolidacni Banka a.s. and the privatisation agency National Property Fund.

Dlouhy said that so far, from an economic point of view, the best offer for a stake in the troubled firm was submitted by Chemapol Group a.s., a fast growing Czech chemical, industrial and trading holding.
"The fact that Chemapol has the best offer today from the price and economic point of view does not mean that other firms will not improve their offers in the tender," said Dlouhy.
He added that he expected interior, defence and foreign affairs ministry experts to sit at the tender steering committee along with his and finance ministry representatives.
The minister said Czech air carrier Ceske Aerolinie a.s. and trading company CIMEX Holding a.s. have also shown interest in the Aero equity expansion plan.

He said that his opinion was based on the fact Aero is the largest domestic military equipment producer and with large export ration and supplies to the army, and should remain controlled by Czech subjects.
The company is currently developing a light military training L-159 jet, equipped with avionics from U.S-based Rockwell Corp. The Czech army has promised to buy 72 of the upgraded jets.
The minister said the government would keep a minority stake in the company at least as long as the L-159s are produced.
